text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Luton Town and Aston Villa at Kenilworth Road!
Following a crushing cup loss to Manchester City in midweek, Luton Town now turn their attention back to avoiding relegation from the Premier League.
A 6-2 thumping in Tuesday's FA Cup tie was the Hatters' fourth straight defeat in all competitions, and they occupy 18th place in the top-flight table.
Though they have proven tough to beat on home turf this season, Rob Edwards' side have conceded 19 goals over the course of their last five matches.
3-1 winners when Luton visited Birmingham at the end of October, Aston Villa defeated Nottingham Forest at home last week, recording their first Villa Park victory of 2024.
Although their home form has recently stuttered, Unai Emery's men are unbeaten on the road this year, conceding just one goal in five away fixtures.
The Villans hold a two-point lead over Tottenham in the fourth and final Champions League spot, as things stand.
Kaminski and Townsend come back into Luton's starting XI today, alongside Man City loanee Issa Kabore, who returns after being ineligible to play his parent club earlier this week.

Gabriel Osho is ruled out with a muscular injury, as the Hatters' absence list grows: Mads Andersen, Elijah Adebayo, Albert Sambi Lokonga and Marvelous Nakamba are among several players still unavailable.
After Pau Torres was taken off at half-time against Nottingham Forest with a minor injury, the Spain international is only named on Aston Villa's bench today.
Konsa is back in the starting XI after overcoming a knee problem, but Jhon Duran and Diego Carlos both join long-term absentees Boubacar Kamara, Tyrone Mings and Emi Buendia on the sidelines.
The players are out on the pitch, and kick-off in this Premier League contest is now just moments away!
Luton Town kick off, and we are under way at Kenilworth Road!
Not since 1989 have Aston Villa come away from this venue with a victory, losing on each of their last three visits to the Hatters' headquarters.
Both need three points to aid their respective causes at either end of the table - but who will come out on top?
After an early scare, when Bailey's dangerous cross grazes Ramsey's chest in the box before being cleared away, Luton are enjoying some early possession just inside the opposition half.
At top speed, Mengi races back to snuff out a run through on goal from Ramsey, who was played through by a typically perceptive pass from Douglas Luiz.
The home fans breathe again.
Bell pulls up and then sinks down to the turf, and it looks like he will not be able to continue.
Surely this is a muscular problem.
The defender is walked to the touchline by Luton's medical staff.
Bell's injury sees Ogbene introduced earlier than expected.
A wing-back by trade, the Republic of Ireland star's arrival may mean a shuffle of personnel.
It seems that Doughty will drop into Luton's back three, with Ogbene shuttling up and down the left flank instead.
The latter's contest with Cash could prove interesting.
The home fans are in uproar after Morris is penalised for felling Konsa deep in Villa territory.
The visitors then take their time to clear upfield via a big boot from Martinez.
Aston Villa are keeping possession patiently, as Luton's bright orange jerseys buzz around them.
Then, Ramsey's shove on Barkley gifts the hosts a free-kick in midfield.
Some 40 per cent of the action has taken place in Villa's defensive third so far, although the away side have rarely been under threat.
Emery's men are simply keeping the ball and waiting to strike on the break.

SAVE! Back in the starting XI today, Kaminski dives across to his left, tipping away Ramsey's stinging shot from an angle! McGinn fed Villa's home-grown starlet with a smart pass, but the Luton goalkeeper was equal to it!
Ramsey is temporarily withdrawn, having picked up a knock; in his absence, Douglas Luiz arrives unmarked in the box but only steers a free header well wide of the target.
Villa are back to 11 men following Ramsey's return, and they'll be aiming to build upon a couple of half-chances they've had so far.
They've taken three shots at goal, while Luton are yet to record one.
Mengi tussles with Watkins near the halfway line and brings the England striker down, conceding a free-kick.
Villa's top scorer is making his 50th successive Premier League appearance today.
Tight to the right byline, Watkins looks up towards the centre of Luton's area but can only find the gloves of Kaminski, who completes a comfortable catch from the forward's tame cross.

SHARP STOP! McGinn, Bailey and Watkins combine, and the latter reaches the edge of the area before unleashing a firm strike at goal! Again, Kaminski stands firm and palms it away! That's an Aston Villa corner.

VILLA IN FRONT! Reaching 20 goals for the season, Watkins rises highest at the near post, meeting Bailey's curling corner with a powerful header angled into the top-right corner! Kaminski had no chance on this occasion, and Aston Villa take another first-half lead: 1-0!
From the right side, Bailey sends over a corner-kick to opening goalscorer Watkins in the centre of Luton's area.
After conceding the opening goal at Kenilworth Road this season, Luton have gone on to take just one point from eight Premier League games.
Now trailing to a well-drilled Aston Villa side, they are really up against the odds today.
Luton have not been fazed by going a goal down, as they are enjoying a little more possession now.
Given their recent defensive problems, they perhaps need to steady the ship rather than chase an immediate equaliser.
Following his earlier injury, Ramsey cannot continue.
January signing Rogers comes on to replace him.
A second successive Villa corner, this time taken short by Bailey in a pre-planned routine, ultimately ends with Lenglet steering McGinn's inswinging cross well over the crossbar.
There's more injury woe now, this time for Luton Town.
Mengi is hobbling around with what looks like an ankle problem, and the action is paused while the centre-back receives treatment.
CLOSE! Although not moving freely, Mengi is now back in place.
Soon after his re-introduction, Watkins zips a low shot across the face of goal from the edge of the area.
It barely brushes the post on its way wide!

Aston Villa have scored more first-half goals than any other side in the Premier League this season (28), while only champions Manchester City (13) have led at half-time more often than the Villans (12).
They're on course to hold an advantage at the interval today, too.
Burke fells Morgan and becomes the first player booked today.

ASTON VILLA SCORE? Although immediately flagged for offside, Watkins finishes calmly from just inside the box, and after a brief delay the VAR intervenes with a potential goal check! Could Villa be about to lead 2-0?

WATKINS STRIKES AGAIN! Slipping clear of Luton's wide-open defence, Watkins latches on to a superb long pass by Douglas Luiz, takes one touch and then coolly slams the ball home via the right-hand post! It's a clinical finish, and the VAR ultimately decides that he was onside: it's 2-0 to Aston Villa before the break!
Displaying quick thinking, Douglas Luiz drops a long free-kick over Luton's defence to release Watkins, who then scores.
Luton are yet to have a shot in today's game, and it's apparent that confidence is seeping away by the minute.
They simply can't stop leaking goals at the moment.
Villa are now in cruise mode.

SUPER SAVE! Kaminski keeps Luton in it! Substitute Rogers cuts inside and fires a powerful shot at goal, but the goalkeeper rises high to fingertip it over the crossbar by the finest of margins! That could have finished it from a Villa point of view.
For bringing down Clark with a minor shove, Douglas Luiz goes into the referee's notebook.
In the second minute of at least seven added for several stoppages, Chong drills the ball wildly over the top from a tight angle on the left.
There's been a total lack of composure in the final third so far, which will disappoint Luton boss Edwards.
Watkins tries to link up with Bailey on the right side of Luton's area, but a vital interception by Ogbene just stops the Jamaican winger receiving it.

MISS! After a period of head-tennis just outside Aston Villa's six-yard box, Townsend arrives on the scene and plants a headed effort over the crossbar! That's as close as Luton have come to scoring so far - and it wasn't that close!
Butler brings down Ogbene, in an intriguing battle between two speedy wingers - he's shown a yellow card by the referee.
Bailey shoots straight at Kaminski from mid-range, then Barkley strikes a 20-yard free-kick into Villa's defensive wall at the other end soon after.
That's all for the first half.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-2 ASTON VILLA
Another display of clinical finishing by Watkins puts Aston Villa 2-0 ahead at the interval, as listless Luton Town struggle to make many openings at Kenilworth Road.
Villa's first came via a header from a set-piece, before Watkins beat both the hosts' offside trap and the assistant's flag to score a VAR-awarded second.

Emery's men have had more of the ball and are in double figures for attempts, leaving the Hatters trailing in their wake and looking likely to suffer a fifth straight defeat - Villa have won 11 from 12 when leading at half-time in the Premier League this season.

In fact, Aston Villa have only ever lost two Premier League matches after leading by two or more goals at half-time, going on to taste victory 61 times and drawing three; however, one of those instances occurred earlier this season, against Manchester United.
It's asking a lot for Luton to replicate the Red Devils' fantastic fightback on that occasion.
Villa kick off, and we are back under way!

Kabore raids forward and earns his side a free-kick high on the right flank; however, Barkley's delivery from the set-piece just beats the head of Burke in the centre and Aston Villa clear their lines.
Kaminski completes a routine stop in the centre of his goal, after Rogers releases Watkins on the left side of Luton's area and the England striker's tame effort rolls towards the target.
Kabore causes Villa more problems out wide, as Rogers is forced into a clumsy challenge that sees him shown a yellow card.
An outswinging corner from the left, taken by set-piece specialist Doughty, briefly causes some concern for the visitors' defence.
It ultimately comes to nothing, but this is much better from Luton, who have started the second half brightly.
Having made his debut in midweek, Hashioka now comes on to replace Townsend.
That could see Doughty shift forward, reverting to the wing-back position.
The Hatters are still enjoying their best spell of the match, and the home fans are responding with some raucous support.
Cash is drawn into a challenge on Chong, conceding a free-kick around 20 yards from goal.
JUST OVER! Doughty's free-kick from the left is swung over towards Morris at the back post, but the striker's looping header only finds the top of the net.
Luton are totally on top now - what a turnaround from their tepid first-half performance!
Another raking long ball by Douglas Luiz almost opens up Luton on the counter, but Bailey can't quite reach the ball despite his express pace.
Of course, the hosts' pursuit of a way back into this game will leave them open to conceding again.
Rogers again tussles with Kabore, who duly goes down to the ground.
It's just a free-kick for Luton, but the Villa substitute must be careful not to get drawn into more rash challenges - he's already been booked.
Clark slips through Ogbene on the right side of Aston Villa's area, but the latter's low cross is blocked away to relative safety.
The Villans have been on the back foot since half-time; their two-goal lead remains intact, though.
Tielemans falters when in a good shooting position just outside the box, and Villa's first attack for some time ultimately comes to nothing.
Soon after, Lenglet is forced to hack a low cross behind for a Luton corner.
LUTON PULL ONE BACK! Doughty's inswinging corner is almost met by Morris at the back post, but Burke instead deflects the ball towards Chong.
The latter does not hesitate to fire in from close range, and that reduces the Hatters' deficit: it's just 2-1 to Aston Villa with more than 20 minutes remaining!
Popping up in a packed penalty area, Burke guides the ball to goalscorer Chong.
Having now scored for a 14th straight Premier League game, Luton Town have also attempted 23 crosses in this match so far - already higher than their season average of 22.2 in the top flight.
They've certainly benefited from Doughty moving back into his favoured position on the left flank.
Emery cuts a concerned figure near the touchline, as his team are unable to push forward and halt Luton's tide of momentum.
Perhaps a change of plan is needed?

LUTON LEVEL!!! It's 2-2 at Kenilworth Road! What a comeback from the Hatters! A typically precise delivery from Doughty's right-wing free-kick finds Morris, who then slots the ball into the bottom corner, sending the Luton fans wild with delight! That sets up a grandstand finale now!

events.action: slots the ball into the bottom corner

text: Crossing brilliantly from a free-kick, set-piece specialist Doughty adds another assist to his record.
Morris has now contributed to goals in each of his last four home games in the Premier League - three of his own and one assist.
What a valuable contribution that could be to Luton's fight for survival.
SAVE! An inspired Morris rises high above Cash to steer a header at goal, but it's directed straight at Martinez, who keeps it out! Villa stay level, but they are reeling now!
Ever the villain - as well as a Villan - Martinez draws boos for hanging on to the ball for longer than needed, as Aston Villa try to quell Luton's momentum.
They've simply had no answer to the hosts' revival since half-time.
Maybe a little later than required, Emery makes some changes.
The first of four substitutions sees Moreno replaced by Digne at left-back.
Tielemans makes way for Zaniolo.
A first-half substitute due to Ramsey's injury, Rogers is now replaced himself: Iroegbunam comes on.
Finally, Bailey is withdrawn and Diaby will replace him.
Luton continue to press for a late winner, as Martinez is required to cut out another Doughty set-piece delivery inside his six-yard box.
Whatever the outcome today, ex-Villa player Edwards will surely be proud of his team's resilience.
The game is paused momentarily, as goalscorer Chong appears to have sustained an injury to his ankle.
There's a brief lull while he's assessed by the medics.
Having netted Luton's first goal, Chong is now forced off by injury; long-serving Mpanzu replaces him.
Flagged for offside straight afterwards, Morris flashes a first-time shot across goal from the right side of Villa's area, with two colleagues arriving just too late to tap it in.
The Hatters keep on creating chances.
Under pressure from the irrepressible Morris, Digne has to concede a corner when Doughty sends over a hanging cross from the left wing.
Martinez then plucks the subsequent set-piece delivery out of the evening air without too much trouble.

VILLA SNATCH IT! Heartbreak for Luton! Villa finally gain some sustained possession in opposition territory, and their substitutes bail them out! Diaby delivers a cross from the right for fellow Frenchman Digne, who nods past Kaminski at the back post! How cruel for the Hatters, who have fought back so valiantly since half-time: it's 3-2 to Villa!
Making a major impact from off the bench, Diaby crosses for Digne to set up Aston Villa's third - and potentially winning - goal.
There will be at least five minutes of stoppage time - can Luton come back again and steal a late point?
After a delay, the referee finally produces a yellow card for Villa substitute Zaniolo.
Having clashed heads in an aerial challenge, potential match-winner Digne is down on the turf nursing an injury.
That will see stoppage time extended, but at least he's able to return to his feet following treatment.
After Barkley's low shot is hacked hurriedly behind by Cash for a corner, Mengi heads well over the crossbar from the subsequent set-piece by Doughty.
Is that Luton's last chance gone?
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 2-3 ASTON VILLA

After letting a two-goal lead slip and then looking likely to concede a third, Aston Villa steal maximum points with a late winner at Kenilworth Road, leaving Luton Town empty-handed despite their superb second-half revival.

The Villans were cruising thanks to Watkins' brace before the break, but their hosts fought back strongly, as Chong and Morris replied, following a barrage of crosses and set-piece deliveries from Luton's widemen.
Finally, substitute Digne slipped free to head home Villa's third goal, which lifts them five points clear of Tottenham in the race for a top-four finish - albeit having played one game more.
Meanwhile, the Hatters remain four points adrift of safety, ahead of next week's visit to fellow strugglers Crystal Palace.
Having escaped with victory today, a big week lies ahead for Aston Villa, who visit Amsterdam for a Europa Conference League tie with Ajax before hosting Spurs three days later.
That's all from our live Premier League coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
